# Francis Ngannou

## Background
Francis Ngannou is a Cameroonian-French mixed martial artist and boxer born on September 5, 1986, in Batié, Cameroon. He's widely regarded as one of the most powerful punchers in combat sports history.

## Early Life
- Grew up in poverty in Cameroon
- Worked various jobs including sand mining before pursuing combat sports
- Made a dangerous journey to Europe as an immigrant, spending time in Spain and France
- Began training in boxing and MMA relatively late, in his early 20s

## MMA Career

### UFC Run (2015-2023)
- Debuted in UFC in December 2015
- Known for devastating knockout power - holds several UFC records for punching force
- Notable victories include knockouts of Alistair Overeem, Junior dos Santos, and Cain Velasquez
- **UFC Heavyweight Champion** (March 2021 - January 2023)
- Won title by knocking out Stipe Miocic at UFC 260
- Successfully defended against Derrick Lewis at UFC 265
- Left UFC in early 2023 due to contract disputes

### Fighting Style
- Devastating punching power (measured over 129,000 units on UFC's PowerKube)
- Improved grappling and wrestling over his career
- Reach advantage at 83 inches
- Known for first-round knockouts

## Boxing Career
- Transitioned to professional boxing in 2023
- Signed with PBC (Premier Boxing Champions)
- Made headlines with competitive performance against Tyson Fury in October 2023, losing a controversial split decision
- Demonstrated his boxing skills translated well from MMA

## Personal Characteristics
- Speaks multiple languages (French, English, and local Cameroonian languages)
- Known for his humble personality despite his fearsome fighting reputation
- Advocate for fighter rights and fair compensation
- Maintains strong ties to his Cameroonian roots

Ngannou represents one of the most successful crossover stories in modern combat sports, going from extreme poverty to becoming a world champion in MMA and competing at the highest level of boxing.
